payload.body:
fix:2:0 — round 0. Both blocking issues are the same single red, and I can now name its cause exactly; the earlier session's diagnosis of it was wrong in a way that matters, so here is the corrected one.

CORRECTION to the earlier note (and to this exam's own header): the trigger is NOT `render-move.test.ts`'s `process.chdir`. `repoRoot` there is `resolve(import.meta.dir, "../../..")` — the real repository root — and `bun test` already runs from it, so those two `chdir`s (lines 508 and 855) are no-ops. Nothing to do with a temporary root.

The actual cause, reproduced deterministically in ONE file with no chdir anywhere:

  await bundleOf(resolve(repoRoot, "client/index.html"), <that html>)   // packages/tinyapp-exam/src/render-move.ts
  await loadContext()                                                   // packages/tinyapp-lint/src/context.ts
  -> error: Cannot find module "@/components/ui/button" from client/src/TodoInput.tsx

Reverse the two calls and it is green, and a second `loadContext()` after the bundle is red again. So: `bundleOf` registers the `tinyapp-tsconfig-paths` plugin (`pathsPlugin`, render-move.ts:311-329) through `Bun.build({plugins})`. Under Bun 1.4.0 that `onResolve({filter: /^@\//})` leaks out of the build into the process-wide runtime resolver, and at runtime it answers `undefined` and takes Bun's own tsconfig-paths handling down with it — so every later runtime `import()` of a `client/src` module in that process fails on `@/…`. `loadContext()` does exactly that (`await import(resolve(root, page))` -> StaticPage.tsx -> TodoItem -> TodoInput -> `@/components/ui/button`).

That is why `bun test packages/tinyapp-lint packages/tinyapp-exam` is red while either package alone is green, and why it is FLAKY rather than always red: it is purely an ordering effect, and Bun's file order varies run to run. Measured here, `bun test packages/tinyapp-exam/test/render-move.test.ts packages/tinyapp-lint/test/references.test.ts` was 4-fail in 5 of 6 runs.

Confirmed pre-existing and not this task's: same 5-run measurement in a clean worktree at BASE (d965df9) — 4 fail, 5 times out of 5. Nothing in this task's file scope is in the chain: the poisoning call is in `packages/tinyapp-exam/src/render-move.ts` and the whole of `packages/tinyapp-exam` is required byte-identical to BASE by this task's own `Check: git diff --quiet` line; the four files that go red under it are `packages/tinyapp-lint/test/*.test.ts`, which are sibling task 3's; and the leg that spawns the command is `tests/state-exams/styled-page.test.ts` leg (f), which is in no task's FILES. Converting my own `@/components/ui/input` import to a relative one would not help — `TodoInput.tsx` is reached first and is not mine either.

So both of the referee's items are the same one failure and it is out of reach:
- `Run: bun test tests/state-exams/type-due-date.test.ts tests/state-exams/styled-page.test.ts` -> 44 pass / 1 fail, the 1 being styled-page leg (f).
- `bun test tests/state-exams/type-tags.test.ts` -> 13 pass / 1 fail, the 1 being leg (c), which spawns that same Run line.

Everything else on this tree is green and stays green: type-due-date 11/11, type-tags legs (a) and (b) 13/13 (the stateExam move, the expected-file pin, and every per-row pin on `#tags-0`/`#tags-1`), `bun run lint:ui` 0, `bun run typecheck` 0, `bun run lint:state` 0 findings over 24 snapshots and 28 exams, and the frozen-path `git diff --quiet` clean against BASE.

I did not edit the exam. The examiner returned leg (c) as unsatisfiable and said not to weaken it, and the instructions say a peer exam red for a reason other than the missing implementation is reported, not edited around. Reporting it as `exam:` + `plan-defect:` concerns and setting work.attention to needs-human: the one-line fix is in a path this plan freezes (scope `pathsPlugin` to the build, or restore Bun's resolver after `Bun.build`), so only the operator can unfreeze it.
